title: After eating
hookLine: praise to Allah who fed me this without power from me (Abu Dawud; Tirmidhi)
tomorrow: worry and grief: are they the same thing?

lines: A PLATE FROM SOMEONE ELSE'S HANDS.
cards: A plate set in front of you by someone else's hands. Maybe a friend's mother who wouldn't let you help, or pay, or even carry your dish to the sink. Maybe a cafeteria tray, cooked by people you'll never see.
Either way the meal arrives already made. The Prophet ﷺ gave a line for the end of it: praise to Allah, who fed me this and provided it for me, without any power from me and without any strength.

teach.b: It's in Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi: alhamdu lillahil-ladhi at'amani hadha wa razaqanihi min ghayri hawlin minni wa la quwwah.
And the hadith adds: whoever says it, their past sins are forgiven. That's a lot to hang on one sentence after lunch, which is the surprise worth telling a friend tonight.
Look at the phrase 'without any power from me'. It's honest in a way that's easy to skip.

Even a meal you cooked yourself came from seeds you didn't make, rain you didn't send, hands you'll never meet: a farmer, a driver, someone stocking a shelf at midnight. The line doesn't erase the cook.
It just doesn't let anyone at the table, the cook included, take all the credit. And it echoes a line from two days ago: la hawla wa la quwwata, no power and no strength except by Allah.
At the door, it's said before going out; at the table, after the meal. The same humility, a different moment. In a week of hard things, it does one more job.
It gives you something true to say when you've eaten far from your own kitchen, at a stranger's table, or alone.
Fed without my power: looked after anyway.

how: Muslims say bismillah before eating and, after finishing, a line of praise such as this one, quietly, at the table.

o: praise after a meal, for food given without your power
thanks said to the host when a meal ends
a blessing said over food before the first bite

games.q: the line, piece by piece — tap the pairs.
p: the same humility, at the door

s: the after-meal line is only for food you cooked
it praises God for food given without any power from me, whoever cooked.
the hadith attaches forgiveness of past sins to it
the line means the cook deserves no thanks
it doesn't erase the cook; it keeps anyone from taking all the credit.

games.q: your roommate cooks dinner for you both, and you say the after-meal line. she asks, 'so you're thanking God and not me?' what's the honest answer?
o: 'yes, only God; you didn't really do anything.'
'both. the line keeps anyone from taking all the credit, and thank you, really.'
'it's just a habit; it doesn't really mean anything.'
games.why: fed without my power doesn't erase the cook; it puts every pair of hands, hers too, inside the gift.

practice: If you have anything to eat or drink nearby, take one small bite or sip and let it sit on your tongue. Trace it back as far as you can: who carried it, who grew it, what weather it needed.
Then say the line, or just its heart: fed without my power.

wordCard.voice: After eating: praise to Allah who fed me this and provided it, without any power or strength from me.

orig.note: Arabic: He fed me; from the after-meal line.

carryVoice: Your line: fed without my power. Looked after, even at a stranger's table. Plate cleared.

sources.ref: Sunan Abu Dawud 4023; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3458 (the line after eating)
